messages:
alex: Heads-up — customer A asked for exact control over rerank `top_k` behavior and wants guarantees around score normalization and truncation. They want a firm GA date if we can meet their SLAs. Need to triage scope.
maya: Can you paste their asks? is this the same as the earlier `top_k` truncation thread?
alex: Not identical — they want ability to: set an absolute `top_k` cap, choose between `soft` vs `hard` truncation, and opt into per-request score rescaling to a 0-1 range. Example payload they proposed: 
```json
{
  "candidates": [{"id":"c1","text":"..."}, ...],
  "signal": "click_rate",
  "top_k": 50,
  "truncation":"hard",
  "normalize":"minmax"
}
```
raj: Two quick flags: 1) hard truncation + large top_k increases token IO, might blow our p99. 2) normalization strategy implies we commit to an algorithm (minmax vs softmax) and the downstream expectations.
sam: Agree. For GA we'd need perf targets: p50/p95 latency and cost per 1k requests with avg candidate sizes. Also backcompat behavior if clients don't pass flags.
emily: From product standpoint customers want: predictable cost, stable rank order, and no regressions in A/B. We should define rollout gates: API contract, perf within 20% of current, fairness/regression checks on eval set.
alex: Proposal: MVP API surfaces — 
1) `top_k` integer with server cap (configurable per-account)
2) `truncation` enum: `none | soft | hard` (soft = drop after soft threshold by heuristic)
3) `normalize` enum: `none | minmax | softmax` (default none)
We default to server-side caps and a warning in response when client requests exceed limits.
maya: Implementation notes from runtime: `softmax` requires logit access; for some models we only get raw scores from an external reranker. Also quantization could change score ranges — need a test harness.
raj: For perf: if top_k > 20 we recommend batch path; else low-latency path. Need telemetry to see distribution. Can we add a per-request hint `preferred_path: low_latency|batch`?
sam: Telemetry + rollout plan: canary to 5% accounts with synthetic load, run eval suite comparing ordering against baseline using NDCG / pairwise flips. Gate if flips > 3% or NDCG delta < -0.02.
emily: Customer asks for SLA terms — product suggests we commit only to latency SLO for default configs. For non-defaults (high top_k + hard truncation) mark as best-effort or require dedicated/dedicated tier.
alex: Decision check: Is the team comfortable shipping API with `minmax` and `softmax` options, and server-side account caps, with canary rollout + eval gates?
maya: Yes but we need a compatibility mode: if client sends `normalize` and we can't compute it, return `normalize_applied:false` and `scores: original` plus a warning in `meta`.
raj: Also add `score_version` in response so downstream can detect algorithm changes.
sam: Acceptance checklist (short):
- API contract doc + examples
- perf benchmarks for top_k=[5,20,50] on p50/p95
- eval runbook + baseline comparisons
- telemetry: top_k distribution, path chosen, normalize failures
- feature flag + canary config
emily: Timeline ask from sales: customer wants GA in 8 weeks. Engineering estimate?
maya: Narrow MVP scope might fit 6–8 weeks if we reuse existing batch infra; full normalization for all model types might take longer.
alex: Action items: @maya draft API spec w/ examples, @raj perf matrix + infra risk, @sam eval gating script, @emily draft customer comms and SLA note. I'll assemble launch criteria doc after updates.
ops-bot: deploy-notify — created ticket RF-1372 for "rerank: top_k/truncation/normalization MVP" assigned to eng.
emily: Thanks — we'll sync tomorrow at 10 to set the canary cadence. :thumbsup:
raj: One more: add an opt-in `preserve_score` boolean so some customers can get raw scores alongside normalized ones. Low effort and helpful.
maya: Good call. I'll add it to the spec.
alex: Great, closing for now. We'll reconvene after the spec draft. :calendar:
